proofs.proof_tex:
We first prove that the structural charts are exhaustive, including every support face. Positivity of the selected table gives \(v_e(z)>0\) for every cell \(e\) and instrument value \(z\). If \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\), the defining equality
\[
 T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top} \tag{3}
\]
expresses \(T_e\) as a sum of two rank-one matrices. Hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(T_e)\leq 2 \tag{4}
\]
at every point of either cycle fiber. A cell rank exceeding two therefore makes every chart, and hence the relevant cycle fiber, empty. Rank zero is impossible because every entry of \(T_e\) is positive.

Fix a rank-two cell. Since \(v_e(z)>0\), its normalized columns
\[
 c_{ez}=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)} \tag{5}
\]
are defined. Equation (3) and \(a_{ei}(z)+a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)\) give
\[
 c_{ez}=\lambda_{ez}b_i+(1-\lambda_{ez})b_j,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{ez}=\frac{a_{ei}(z)}{v_e(z)}\in[0,1]. \tag{6}
\]
Rank two forces \(b_i\neq b_j\), so all observed points in (5) and both endpoints lie on one affine line. Conversely, if the endpoints occur on that line and contain every \(c_{ez}\) in their closed segment, choose a coordinate \(h_e\) separating the endpoints. Then the unique coefficients are
\[
 a_{ei}(z)=v_e(z)
 \frac{c_{ez}(h_e)-b_j(h_e)}{b_i(h_e)-b_j(h_e)},
 \qquad
 a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z). \tag{7}
\]
The denominator in (7) is nonzero by the pivot choice, and the segment condition makes both coefficients nonnegative. The two endpoint orders are exactly the orientations proved exhaustive in \(\mathrm{thm:rank\text{-}two\text{-}orientation\text{-}atlas}\). For each \(z\), the positive sum in (6) permits exactly three support alternatives: the first coefficient is zero, the second is zero, or both are positive. These alternatives exhaust every rank-two coefficient face.

For a rank-one cell, \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\) proves that the four \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes are disjoint and exhaustive. In mode \(\mathrm L\), the inactive endpoint \(b_i\) remains unrestricted except for its simplex and shared-vertex constraints; mode \(\mathrm R\) is symmetric. Mode \(\mathrm E\) retains the entire coordinatewise split vector, including its zero, interior, and upper-endpoint faces. Thus coincident endpoints, inactive response rows, and forced zeros are not removed by a rank or division argument.

Take the product of the four local mode lists and use one common endpoint variable \(b_i\) at the two incidences of response type \(i\). Fix the endpoint and coefficient support states counted by the local modes. Every endpoint equality or inequality, line incidence, and pivot condition required by a mode is retained as a polynomial sign atom in that coarse structural template; a remaining finite alternative is retained as a Boolean combination of those atoms rather than counted as a new structural template. A denominator is cleared only after its nonzero sign has been recorded. Equations (6)--(7), the rank-two orientation theorem, and the rank-one normal-form lemma show that every point of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) belongs to at least one chart. Direct substitution into (3), the endpoint simplex equations, and \(a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e\) proves that every chart point belongs to \(\mathcal C_A(T)\). Consequently,
\[
 \bigcup_\chi X_\chi=\mathcal C_A(T). \tag{8}
\]

For design B, fix a chart in (8) and a positive projective vector \(\rho\). At every response type, \(\mathrm{thm:iv\text{-}residual\text{-}forest}\) proves the exhaustive alternatives: both incident residuals vanish; exactly one vanishes, in which case the branch is infeasible; or both are nonzero and negatively proportional. In the active case the first nonzero residual coordinate is a legal pivot, and its two possible signs form a finite refinement. The resulting positive margin ratios propagate from one positive scale on each forest component. If all four links form the cycle, path consistency is equivalent to the single product-one equation. Scale positivity and the margin normalization give all and only the positive margins. Finally, enumerating an ordered pair \(z<z'\) and the sign of
\[
 q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z) \tag{9}
\]
is exhaustive for relevance. The residual-forest theorem therefore yields
\[
 \bigcup_\chi X_\chi=\mathcal C_B(T) \tag{10}
\]
for the design-B refinements.

The supplied population margin does not occur in (8), so cycle feasibility alone cannot certify a design-A full SCM. The first test in the corrected \(\mathrm{def:atlas\text{-}handle}\), together with \(\mathrm{lem:design\text{-}a\text{-}fiber\text{-}nonempty\text{-}criterion}\), gives
\[
 \mathcal F_A(p,m)\neq\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}
 \ \text{and}\ 
 \bigcup_\chi X_\chi\neq\varnothing. \tag{11}
\]
Thus a supplied margin outside the strict interior is reported as incompatible before sampling or lifting. In design B, (10) and the onto part of \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) give
\[
 \mathcal F_B(p)\neq\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bigcup_\chi X_\chi\neq\varnothing. \tag{12}
\]

Assume now that the appropriate union is nonempty. The target map is polynomial in the chart variables because
\[
 \tau_C(b,a)=
 \left(\sum_z a_{11,2}(z),\sum_z a_{00,2}(z)\right). \tag{13}
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem:one\text{-}sample\text{-}all\text{-}chart\text{-}rigidity}\) to the finite family in (8) or (10), with \(f=\tau_C\). It first supplies one \(x_0\), then decides exactly the one-copy refinements (2). The lemma proves
\[
 \tau_C\!\left(\bigcup_\chi X_\chi\right)=\{\tau_C(x_0)\}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{every refinement in (2) is empty}. \tag{14}
\]
This comparison is global: a point on a disconnected component or another support face still belongs to some \(X_\chi\) and is tested against the same fixed \(t_0\). Hence connected-component enumeration is unnecessary for the decision.

The initial sample has a real-univariate representation over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), and (13) places \(t_0\) in its real algebraic coordinate field. The refinements are therefore effective over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\). If all are empty, the exact encoding of \(t_0\) is the rigid output. The compiler returns a rational expression over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only if field arithmetic constructs one; otherwise it retains the real-univariate and Thom representation. If a refinement is nonempty, the cited sampler gives \(x_1\) and (2) gives \(\tau_C(x_1)\neq\tau_C(x_0)\). Equations (8) or (10) make both samples legal cycle points, and \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) produces two full SCMs with identical observables and, in design A, the same supplied margins. Each feasibility formula contains only the one variable block \(x\); \(t_0\) is a fixed algebraic coefficient. This proves the theorem.

In design A, \(\mathrm{lem:design\text{-}a\text{-}fiber\text{-}nonempty\text{-}criterion}\) proves
\[
 \mathcal F_A(p,m)\neq\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}
 \ \text{and}\ 
 \mathcal C_A(T)\neq\varnothing. \tag{15}
\]
Thus an invalid supplied margin must be rejected even if the normalized cycle charts are nonempty. In design B, the surjectivity assertion of \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal F_B(p)\neq\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C_B(T)\neq\varnothing. \tag{16}
\]
Because an empty target set has cardinality zero, the failures in (15)--(16) are incompatible and non-rigid under \(\mathrm{def:target\text{-}rigidity}\).

On a nonempty fiber, the same lift lemma preserves the target and is onto, so
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal T_A(p,m)
 &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},\\
 \mathcal T_B(p)
 &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{17}
\]
The structural equalities in \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) replace each cycle fiber in (17) by the finite union of its charts. Its one-sample/all-chart equivalence (14) then proves that the relevant set in (17) is a singleton exactly when every chartwise unequal-target refinement is empty. This establishes necessity and sufficiency, including disconnected charts and comparisons across support faces, without connected-component enumeration.

The mixed-support theorem also proves the stated field-relative output discipline. If a refinement is feasible, it supplies cycle points \(x_0,x_1\) with unequal values. Equation (17) and the cycle-to-SCM lift turn these into legal full SCMs with the same observed input and, in design A, the same supplied \(m\). If both points satisfy all strict inequalities of interior support charts, \(\mathrm{lem:interior\text{-}cycle\text{-}to\text{-}positive\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) makes every response mass, proxy and instrument kernel, treatment probability, and selection probability strictly interior. That lemma makes no such assertion when either witness lies on a support face, so the boundary qualification is exact.

Condition 1 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki factorizes the selected joint mass as
\[
 p(x,y,s,w,z,u)=p(s\mid x,y)p(y\mid x,u)p(x\mid z,u)
 p(w\mid u)p(z\mid u)p(u). \tag{18}
\]
In the present model, response consistency makes \(p(y\mid x,u)\) the deterministic kernel encoded by the four values of \(U\); outcome-dependent selection gives the first factor in (18); proxy exclusion gives \(p(w\mid u)\); and the treatment and second-proxy mechanisms in \(P_{\vartheta}\) give the remaining factors. Thus every law in \(\mathfrak M\) is the finite four-response-type specialization of (18).

The definition of \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) adds to this factorization the constraints
\[
 P_{\vartheta}(E,W,Z\mid S=1)=p,
 \qquad P_{\vartheta}(E)=m. \tag{19}
\]
Hence it is a fixed-population-margin subfiber of the Condition-1 model; fixing \(m\) does not remove any conclusion that holds pointwise for every member of the larger regular fiber. Let \(R_A(p)\) denote the PN/PS pair computed by Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). By \(\mathrm{lem:shingaki\text{-}yoshida\text{-}kuroki\text{-}regular\text{-}identification}\), Conditions 2--3 imply
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)=R_A(p) \tag{20}
\]
for every \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\). Compatibility makes this set nonempty, so (20) yields
\[
 \mathcal T_A(p,m)=\{R_A(p)\}. \tag{21}
\]
The full-rigidity theorem must therefore return \(R_A(p)\).

For design B, instrument exogeneity gives \(p(z\mid u)=g(z)\), response consistency gives the same deterministic outcome kernel, and the mechanism defining \(P_{\vartheta}\), proxy exclusion, and outcome-dependent selection yield
\[
 p(x,y,s,w,z,u)=p(s\mid x,y)p(y\mid x,u)p(x\mid z,u)
 p(w\mid u)g(z)p(u), \tag{22}
\]
which is equation (13) of the cited paper. The definition of \(\mathcal F_B(p)\) additionally imposes \(Z\not\!\perp X\), exactly the relevance restriction. On the regular domain of Conditions 2--3, \(\mathrm{lem:shingaki\text{-}yoshida\text{-}kuroki\text{-}regular\text{-}iv\text{-}identification}\) applies directly to (22). If its observable PN/PS pair is denoted by \(R_B(p)\), then
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)=R_B(p)
 \quad\text{for every }\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p),
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_B(p)=\{R_B(p)\}. \tag{23}
\]
Again the full-rigidity theorem forces \(\mathscr A\) to return that same value.

Outside Conditions 2--3, no use is made of (20) or (23). Instead, \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) exhausts the rank-one and rank-two modes, all coefficient faces, equal endpoints, inactive endpoints, and every residual-forest state. The full-rigidity theorem then supplies either the common exact value or target-changing legal lifts on every compatible law. Equations (15)--(16) ensure that incompatibility is detected separately. Thus the new conclusion is precisely the stated singular/boundary classification and does not modify the domain or formula of the published regular result.

We verify the structural count, the sequential algebraic-degree multiplication, and the rational-height recurrence in the order used by the compiler.

A proxy endpoint \(b_i\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}\) has a nonempty support, so it has at most \(2^{\ell}-1\) labeled support patterns. The four shared response vertices contribute at most
\[
 (2^{\ell}-1)^4. \tag{32}
\]
At a rank-two cell, there are two endpoint orientations. For each of the \(k\) values of \(z\), positivity of \(v_e(z)\) and the equality \(a_{ei}(z)+a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)\) leave three support states: left zero, right zero, or both positive. Thus rank two contributes at most \(2\cdot3^k\) local templates. By \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\), mode \(\mathrm E\) has \(3^k\) coordinatewise split faces, and modes \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm D\) add three more. Allowing either positive-table rank gives at most
\[
 2\cdot3^k+3^k+3=3^{k+1}+3 \tag{33}
\]
local templates per cell. There are four cells, so multiplying (32) by the fourth power of (33) gives \(M_A\).

For design B, every one of the four response links is either a zero-residual link or an active link. An active link records one of \(k-1\) first nonbaseline pivots and one of two pivot signs, giving
\[
 1+2(k-1)=2k-1 \tag{34}
\]
states. A relevance certificate chooses an unordered pair of distinct instrument values and the sign of its nonzero cross-product, giving
\[
 2\binom{k}{2}=k(k-1) \tag{35}
\]
possibilities. The residual-forest exhaustiveness in \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) permits multiplication of these independent coarse labels. This yields \(M_B=M_Ak(k-1)(2k-1)^4\), and addition across the two design outputs yields (24).

For (25), retain four endpoint vectors, requiring \(4\ell\) coordinates, and two incident coefficient vectors in each of four cells, requiring \(8k\). In design B, projective common-instrument and optional joint-treatment auxiliaries require at most \(2k\) more coordinates. Population margins, response masses, component scales, and four residual-transfer scalars require at most twelve further coordinates. Hence the number of variables is at most \(N_0\).

There are \(4k\ell\) table-factorization equations. Endpoint simplex and support conditions use at most \(4\ell+4\) atoms; coefficient simplex, support, and split conditions use at most \(24k+8\); residual definitions and transfer equations use at most \(16k+8\); and retaining every proportionality minor uses at most \(4(k-1)^2\). Shared-instrument equations, normalizations, endpoint incidences, cycle consistency, and signed relevance use fewer than \(20(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1)\) additional atoms. Since \(k\geq2\) and \(\ell\geq3\), their sum is at most \(S_0\).

The table equations are bilinear. A residual \(a_{ei}(z)-\rho_z a_{ei}(z_0)\) has degree at most two. Introducing one transfer scalar makes negative proportionality degree at most three, and the four-link cycle product has degree four. Shared-instrument equations have degree two, relevance has degree at most three after substituting the bilinear definition of \(q^X\), and the remaining atoms have no larger degree. Thus \(D_0=4\). The target in (13) is linear, so adjoining the unequal-target condition adds one atom of degree two and leaves the degree bound \(D_0\) unchanged. This proves (25)--(26).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}sampling\text{-}existential}\) to each structural chart over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). The emptiness-and-sampling phase produces at most \(A_S\) algebraic records per chart. If the union is nonempty, choose the first returned sample \(x_0\) and set \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\). A real-univariate representation of \(x_0\) uses one primitive element \(\alpha\) with
\[
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(\alpha):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
 \leq D_S. \tag{36}
\]
Because \(t_0\) is obtained from \(x_0\) by the linear sums in (13),
\[
 \mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)
 \subseteq\mathbb K_{\zeta}(\alpha),
 \qquad
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
 \leq D_S. \tag{37}
\]

Each of the at most \(M_{k,\ell}\) unequal-target tests is now a one-block existential-realizability problem over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\), with format \((N_0,S_0+1,D_0)\). It creates at most \(A_E\) records. If it returns a witness with primitive coordinate \(\beta\), then
\[
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\beta):
   \mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)]\leq D_E. \tag{38}
\]
The tower law and (37)--(38) give the explicit degree multiplication
\[
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\beta):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
 =
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\beta):\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)]
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
 \leq D_ED_S. \tag{39}
\]
Every output coordinate belongs to the field on the left of (39). Multiplication by such an element is a linear operator on a vector space of dimension at most \(D_ED_S\); its characteristic polynomial annihilates the element. Therefore the minimal polynomial of every output coordinate has degree at most \(D_ED_S\). Passing to its square-free factor and selecting the correct real root by Thom signs or an isolating interval cannot increase that degree. This proves the degree part of (27) by multiplication of extension degrees, not by reapplying a complexity slogan to an already enlarged degree.

There are at most \(M_{k,\ell}\) initial sampling calls and the same number of unequal-target calls. Adding the fixed incompatibility and rigid/nonrigid summary records gives
\[
 2+M_{k,\ell}A_S+M_{k,\ell}A_E=R_{k,\ell}, \tag{40}
\]
which bounds all generated records and therefore all retained outputs.

Put \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\). Equations (24)--(25) imply, for universal constants,
\[
 M_{k,\ell}\leq2^{CQ},
 \qquad N_0\leq CQ,
 \qquad S_0\leq CQ,
 \qquad D_0=4. \tag{41}
\]
The singly exponential bounds in \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}sampling\text{-}existential}\), applied to the two formats in (26), imply
\[
 A_S,D_S,A_E,D_E\leq 2^{CQ^C} \tag{42}
\]
after enlarging \(C\). Substitution of (41)--(42) into (27) and absorption of a fixed product and sum into the exponent prove (28).

For arbitrary real input, selected-cell normalization divides only by \(r_e>0\), and chart normalization divides only by a pivot whose sign is part of the chart. Thus every chart coefficient lies in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). The chart family is finite by (24), and every sampling, existential, sign, and root operation terminates relative to the stated field oracles by the cited algorithmic lemma. This proves field-relative termination.

Suppose now that the coordinates of \(\zeta\) are rational with numerator and denominator lengths at most \(L\). Reconstructing deleted simplex coordinates uses at most \(Q\) additions. Each coefficient in a degree-at-most-four chart atom is obtained using at most \(8Q\) additions or multiplications of these coordinates and recorded pivots. Clearing a product of at most \(8Q\) denominators adds at most \(8Q(L+1)\) bits, and summing at most \(8Q\) resulting terms adds at most \(\lceil\log_2(8Q)\rceil\leq8Q\) bits. Since \(Q\geq1\), the conservative bound
\[
 h_0=64Q^2(L+1) \tag{43}
\]
therefore dominates every initial integer coefficient length. Multiplication by the square of a recorded nonzero denominator preserves a strict sign, so this clearing step does not change a chart.

The integer-height clause of the cited sampling algorithm gives the first recurrence in (29). The coefficients of the unequal-target atom consist of the original chart coefficients and the coordinates of \(t_0\), whose degree and height are bounded by \(D_S\) and \(h_S\). Applying the cited existential height bound over this represented extension gives \(h_E\) in (30). Flattening the tower can be done by multiplication matrices in the vector space of dimension at most \(D_SD_E\): determinants defining characteristic polynomials use at most \(D_SD_E\) products and sums of represented coefficients. The cited square-free and root-isolation algorithms then give the stated \(h_F\). Consequently normalization does not change the degree bound (39).

For each of the two algorithmic stages, the cited height exponent is bounded by \(2^{CQ^C}\) using (41)--(42). The extension-flattening, square-free, and root-isolation exponent is also at most \(2^{CQ^C}\) because \(D_SD_E\leq2^{CQ^C}\). Successive substitutions multiply only a fixed number of such exponents, so, after enlarging \(C\),
\[
 \max\{h_S,h_E,h_F\}
 \leq (h_0+1)^{2^{CQ^C}}
 \leq \bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}, \tag{44}
\]
which is (31). This height statement is separate from the singly exponential record and degree bounds. Square-free normalization and rational root isolation supplied by the cited algorithm give the claimed integer polynomial and isolating data. All loops and rational subroutines are bounded, so the Turing implementation terminates. The executed stages are exactly chart enumeration, chart sampling, and one-copy existential refinement; neither component enumeration nor target projection enters the decision.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(K\) be an effective ordered field and let a semialgebraic subset of a real closed extension of \(K\) be described by a Boolean formula in \(n\) variables involving at most \(s\) polynomial sign conditions of degree at most \(d\). Exact bounded-algebraic-sampling and existential-realizability algorithms decide whether the set is empty and, when it is nonempty, return a real-univariate representation of a sample point with Thom sign data. The same assertion holds after adjoining one further polynomial sign condition and over a finite real algebraic extension of \(K\), with algebraic degree measured relative to that coefficient field. Real-univariate representation, multiplication-matrix, square-free-factorization, Thom-sign, and root-isolation algorithms normalize a finite real-algebraic tower to a square-free univariate representation over the original field without increasing the field degree. There are explicit coordinatewise nondecreasing bounds \(\mathsf{Samp}\) and \(\mathsf{Exist}\) for the numbers of generated algebraic records and their relative algebraic degrees, and corresponding integer-coefficient height bounds, including the final tower-normalization and root-isolation height. For a universal constant \(c\geq 1\), the record-count and relative-degree bounds may be chosen no larger than
\[
 (s+d+2)^{c(n+1)^c},
\]
and, when the integer input coefficients have binary length at most \(h\), the output coefficient and isolating-endpoint lengths may be chosen no larger than
\[
 (h+1)^{(s+d+2)^{c(n+1)^c}}.
\]

source.locator: Algorithms 13.1 and 14.5 and their complexity analyses in Chapters 13--14; real-univariate representations, Thom encodings, multiplication matrices, and integer bit complexity in Chapters 10--14

attestation.note: The stable Springer source and the algorithm locations were checked; the displayed bound is a conservative singly exponential envelope of the cited bounded-algebraic-sampling and existential-realizability bounds.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_J\) be a finite family of one-copy semialgebraic sets over an effective ordered field \(K\), put \(X=\bigcup_{j=1}^J X_j\), and let \(f:X\to\mathbb R^2\) be a polynomial map. There is an exact one-sample/all-chart procedure with the following properties. It first tests every \(X_j\) for emptiness. If \(X\neq\varnothing\), it samples one \(x_0\in X\), puts \(t_0=f(x_0)\), and, over \(K(t_0)\), tests every refinement
\[
 R_j(x_0)=\left\{x\in X_j:
 (f_1(x)-t_{0,1})^2+(f_2(x)-t_{0,2})^2>0\right\}.
\]
Then \(f(X)=\{t_0\}\) if and only if every \(R_j(x_0)\) is empty. If some refinement is nonempty, the procedure samples \(x_1\in R_j(x_0)\), and \(f(x_1)\neq f(x_0)\). The procedure uses no formula containing two independently quantified copies of \(X\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Every \(X_j\) is given by finitely many polynomial sign conditions, so the bounded-algebraic-sampling algorithm in \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}sampling\text{-}existential}\) decides its emptiness. Because the family is finite,
\[
 X=\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 X_j=\varnothing\ \text{for every }j. \tag{1}
\]
If the left side of (1) is false, choose the first nonempty set in the fixed ordering and let its sampled point be \(x_0\). The coordinates of \(t_0=f(x_0)\) lie in the real algebraic field generated by the sample representation. Hence each \(R_j(x_0)\) is a basic semialgebraic set over \(K(t_0)\), obtained from the formula for \(X_j\) by adding one strict polynomial inequality. The existential-realizability part of the cited lemma therefore decides its emptiness and samples it when it is nonempty.

Suppose first that every \(R_j(x_0)\) is empty. For any \(x\in X\), there is a \(j\) with \(x\in X_j\). Since \(x\notin R_j(x_0)\) and a sum of two real squares is nonnegative,
\[
 0=(f_1(x)-t_{0,1})^2+(f_2(x)-t_{0,2})^2
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad f(x)=t_0. \tag{2}
\]
Thus \(f(X)=\{t_0\}\). Conversely, if \(f(X)=\{t_0\}\), the strict inequality defining every \(R_j(x_0)\) is false, so every refinement is empty. Finally, if some \(R_j(x_0)\) is nonempty, its sampled point \(x_1\) satisfies
\[
 (f_1(x_1)-f_1(x_0))^2+(f_2(x_1)-f_2(x_0))^2>0,
\]
which is equivalent to \(f(x_1)\neq f(x_0)\). Only \(x\) is quantified in each refinement; \(x_0\) enters through fixed algebraic coefficients. This proves every assertion.

added_lemmas.statement: Under equation (13), positive selected conditional probabilities, and Conditions 2--3 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026), with an instrument having at least three levels and a proxy having at least three levels, Corollary 1 identifies the conditional counterfactual probabilities and hence PN and PS from the selected observed law in the instrumental-variable-plus-proxy design.

attestation.note: Checked against the PMLR publisher PDF at equation (13) and Corollary 1.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), there is a one-copy structural compiler \(\mathscr A\) with the following properties. It rejects any cell rank exceeding two. A rank-two cell is represented by its two oriented segment modes, refined by all coefficient-support faces. A rank-one cell is represented by the disjoint \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes of \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\), with the \(\mathrm E\) split refined coordinatewise. Products of the four local modes use one shared variable \(b_i\) at each response vertex, fix proxy supports, and retain endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, and guarded nonzero pivots as polynomial sign atoms. Writing \(X_\chi\) for the resulting charts, their union is exactly \(\mathcal C_A(T)\). In design B, adjoining \(\rho\), the zero-residual or active negatively proportional state at every response type, lexicographic nonzero pivots, forest propagation, the active-cycle product-one constraint, positive component scales, normalization, and a signed relevance witness gives a finite chart union exactly equal to \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).

In design A, before declaring compatibility or attempting a lift, \(\mathscr A\) tests \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\). After that test, and directly in design B, it tests all structural charts for emptiness. If all are empty, it reports incompatibility. prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed finite four-response-type selected proxy model, a boundary-complete structural atlas decides PN/PS target rigidity. It exhausts rank-two orientations, all disjoint L/R/E/D rank-one modes, equal-endpoint splits, inactive rows, and the relevant-IV residual forests. After checking the supplied design-A margin, it samples one feasible cycle point and asks every chart whether a different target is realizable. The output is an exact common target, legal same-observable SCM twins, or incompatibility. The published regular formulas transfer by restriction in design A and through equation (13) and Corollary 1 in design B; the new contribution is classification only on additional compatible singular and boundary laws. Fixed-alphabet sample-record and algebraic-degree bounds are singly exponential, while rational height has a separate conservative bound. Exact confidence-fiber coverage remains universal, whereas Wald and Hausdorff equivalence remain confined to their already accepted separated and locally saturated regimes.

project_justification.gap: Published regular proxy formulas do not classify PN/PS constancy when ranks fall, coefficients reach support faces, endpoints coincide, response rows become inactive, or shared-instrument equations couple unknown population margins. General decidability also does not expose the causal response-cycle obstruction or distinguish incompatibility from nonidentification.
project_justification.niche: The four response types form a labeled causal cycle whose target may be rigid while nuisance factorizations vary. Exhaustive rank-two and L/R/E/D edge charts with shared endpoints and residual forests reduce the full fiber to finitely many one-copy semialgebraic sets. One common sampled target can then be compared against every chart without enumerating connected components or introducing a two-copy classifier.
project_justification.fill: The compiler first checks strict supplied-margin compatibility in design A and chart feasibility in both designs. From one feasible sample it performs an unequal-target existential test on every chart, returning an exact target, legal target-changing full SCMs, or incompatibility. The regular anchor is stated exactly as a Condition-1 fixed-margin restriction for design A and an equation-(13) relevant-IV subclass for design B. Its termination theorem counts structural templates and composes only bounded algebraic sampling and existential-realizability bounds, with algebraic degree obtained by multiplying extension degrees and rational height reported separately.

At the selected-law factorization level, the present finite four-type model specializes their Condition 1. The fixed-margin two-proxy fiber is a restriction to which Theorem 1 applies, while the relevant-IV fiber satisfies equation (13) and relevance, so Corollary 1 applies directly. Our contribution does not extend their regular formula or subsume their model; it classifies additional compatible singular and boundary fibers and reports incompatible inputs separately. Shingaki and Kuroki (2023) and Kawakami (2021) provide separate experimental and IV-plus-proxy overlap results under their own conditions. Nonnegative-factorization rigidity work supplies geometric context but not causal target constancy on this labeled response cycle. Rational coefficient and isolating-endpoint height obey the separately displayed power bound and are not advertised as singly exponential.
